review: The hymn is Song 5:10–16 applied to Christ: 1:1 keeps the cedar of Lebanon (Song 5:15, כְּאַרְזֵי לְבָנוֹן), 1:2 the marble pillars (שֹׁהַם — the Hebrew of 5:15 is עַמּוּדֵי שֵׁשׁ), 1:3 the sweet speech (5:16, מְתַקִּים), and 1:4 'Prince of Peace' is Isa 9:5 (שַׂר־שָׁלוֹם), which the Arabic وَيُدْعَى رَئِيسَ السَّلَام also quotes.

1:2 עַמּוּדֵי שֵׁשׁ רַגְלָיו הֵמָּה — the Arabic سَاقَاهُ عَمُودَا رُخَام has the dual ('his two legs'); Hebrew has no dual here and the Song itself says עַמּוּדֵי שֵׁשׁ, so the construct is kept whole and the legs are supplied as the subject rather than forcing a dual.

2:1 חִכִּיתִי לָשֶׁבֶת — the Arabic اشْتَهَيْتُ الْجُلُوس is 'I longed to sit'; חִכָּה is the waiting verb (Ps 130:5) and לָשֶׁבֶת keeps the sitting, so longing and resting are both present, as in Song 2:3 (בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי).

2:3 מֵנִיחַ יְגֵעִים — the Arabic مُرِيحُ التَّعَابَى is Matt 11:28 (כָּל־הַיְגֵעִים); the participle is kept so the line describes an attribute, and the second clause's מְנַחֵם keeps the Arabic's مُعَزِّي as a separate act.

3:4 הַחֲתֻנָּה — the Arabic الزِّفَاف is the wedding-procession; חֲתֻנָּה is the biblical wedding noun (Song 3:11, בְּיוֹם חֲתֻנָּתוֹ) and is the glossary's fixed word, so the stanza ends at the marriage of the Lamb rather than at a generic feast.
